$comment: GENERATED by tools/derive-factors.mjs - edit that script, not this file.
Emission factors for DeepSeek Harness sessions, in gCO2e per million tokens.
Every entry carries a confidence tier. The only public source of per-query DeepSeek
inference energy is Jegham et al. 2025 (arXiv:2505.09598v6) Table 4, which measures
DeepSeek-V3 and DeepSeek-R1 on DeepSeek’s own Chinese datacenters and on Azure.
It covers no V3.1/V3.2/V4/Pro/Flash checkpoint, and EcoLogits carries no DeepSeek model
at all - so unlike claude-carbon’s Opus/Haiku rows there is no second opinion to

_cache_read_factor.note: Energy of a cache-read token as a fraction of an uncached input token: a prefill residual. DeepSeek’s 0.02 cache-hit PRICE ratio is not an energy ratio and is deliberately not used.

_infrastructure.note: Deployment dominates. Jegham et al. measured the same DeepSeek-V3 at 13.162 Wh on DeepSeek’s own DCs and 3.696 Wh on Azure - a 3.6x gap from PUE, cooling and grid carbon intensity alone.

_default_infrastructure_rationale: DeepSeek Harness runs on DeepSeek’s first-party API, so the operator’s own fleet is the closer assumption. It is also the pessimistic one: roughly 3.6x the Azure reading for identical tokens. Override with DSH_CARBON_INFRA=azure.

models.source: Derived, not measured. Scaled from DeepSeek-V3 on DeepSeek’s own fleet (Jegham et al. v6 Table 4) by active-parameter ratio.
models.derivation: Active parameters from the released config.json: 9.91B routed+shared MLP + 4.28 attention = 14.19B, against V3’s 37B -> 0.3835x. Both prefill FLOPs and decode bytes scale with active parameters, so both terms scale together.
models.caveat: No published measurement exists for this model. fp4 expert weights cut bytes read per decode step below the parameter ratio, which argues the point estimate is high; worse batching or a denser serving stack argues it is low. The band covers that.

models.source: No measurement and no released config. Carried at the Flash point estimate with a much wider band, on the assumption that a Pro tier is the larger sibling on the same fleet.
models.caveat: The weakest row in the table: the multiplier is judgement, not arithmetic. DeepSeek has not published V4-Pro’s architecture, so nothing here is checkable.

fit.note: A per-token model fits V3 well: the three published points lie close to a line through the origin.

models.source: Jegham et al. 2025 (arXiv:2505.09598v6) Table 4: DeepSeek-V3 on DeepSeek’s own datacenters, 2.777 / 8.864 / 13.162 Wh for the three published prompt shapes. Non-negative least squares at CIF 0.6 kgCO2e/kWh, PUE 1.27.
models.caveat: The three points are near-collinear, so the fit cannot separate the two terms: unconstrained least squares drives the input coefficient to -22.14e-6 Wh/token, which is negative and physically meaningless. Output therefore carries essentially all the signal. The input figure here is borrowed from the Azure fit, where it is positive and identifiable, and rescaled to this grid — it is not measured on this fleet. V3.1 and V3.2 match as family aliases; neither checkpoint was measured.

fit.note: Poor fit. R1 costs ~19 Wh even for the smallest prompt, so most of its energy is fixed per query (reasoning traces, long prefill, scheduling), not proportional to tokens. A token-only model therefore under-reports short R1 sessions and over-reports long ones. Reported as an error, not corrected here.

models.source: Jegham et al. 2025 (arXiv:2505.09598v6) Table 4: DeepSeek-R1 on DeepSeek’s own datacenters, 19.251 / 24.596 / 29.078 Wh for the three published prompt shapes.
models.caveat: Same collinearity as V3: the output term absorbs nearly all the fit. R1 is the most energy-intensive DeepSeek row published, which is why it sets the top of the V3 band.

fallback.source: No factor entry matched this model string. The V4.1-Flash point estimate is used so the total is not silently zeroed, and the model is flagged in output.
fallback.caveat: An unmatched model means the report is a guess. Add a row here.

$pricing_note: API-equivalent cost uses DeepSeek list prices, USD per 1M tokens, at the PEAK tariff. Peak is 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC Mon-Fri excluding Chinese public holidays, and is exactly 2x off-peak. A historical report cannot know which tariff applied, so it prices high and says so. Only models DeepSeek currently lists are priced; retired checkpoints carry null and are reported as unpriced rather than guessed.
